clues.text: I was a prophet in Paul's day.
I came down from Jerusalem to Antioch with other prophets.
I said a famine would come on the entire inhabited earth.
After my famine prophecy, the disciples determined to send relief to Judea.
I came down from Judea while Paul was in Caesarea.
I said the Jews in Jerusalem would bind a man and give him into the hands of people of the nations.
I stood up in Antioch and foretold a famine that later came under Claudius.
I took Paul's belt and bound my own feet and hands.
I brought some money and deposited it at the feet of the apostles.
With my wife's knowledge, I secretly held back some of the price of my field.
I sold some property with my wife Sapphira.
On hearing Peter's words, I collapsed and died.
Peter asked why Satan had emboldened me to lie to the holy spirit.
Peter said that while my field remained unsold, it was mine, and after I sold it the proceeds were in my control.
Younger men wrapped me in cloths, carried me out, and buried me.
Great fear came over all who heard about my death.
Peter said I had lied, not to men, but to God.
I died first; about three hours later my wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
I called Saul “brother.”
I laid my hands on Saul so that he might recover sight.
I was a disciple in Damascus.
I answered the Lord: “Here I am, Lord.”
I looked for Saul of Tarsus at the house of Judas.
I said Saul had authority from the chief priests to arrest those calling on the Lord's name.
I told the Lord I had heard of the harm Saul did to the holy ones in Jerusalem.
I was sent to the street called Straight.
After I came to Saul, what looked like scales fell from his eyes.
I entered Judas' house and said Jesus had sent me so Saul might recover sight and be filled with holy spirit.
Paul later said I was devout according to the Law and well-reported-on by the Jews living there.
The Lord told me Saul was a chosen vessel to bear His name to the nations, kings, and the sons of Israel.
I explained that Saul had been chosen to see the righteous one and be a witness to all men.
I raised concerns about Saul's past, but the Lord told me that he was a chosen vessel.
I told Saul to rise, get baptized, and wash his sins away by calling on Jesus' name.
As Paul later recounted, I stood beside him and said: “Saul, brother, regain your sight!”
Paul planted, I watered, but God kept making it grow.
I was an eloquent man well-versed in the Scriptures.
Priscilla and Aquila took me into their company and explained the way of God more accurately.
I was acquainted only with the baptism of John.
I arrived in Ephesus speaking and teaching about Jesus.
I was a Jew, a native of Alexandria.
In Achaia I showed from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
Aglow with the spirit, I taught accurately the things about Jesus.
I had been instructed in the way of Jehovah and began to speak boldly in the synagogue.
In Achaia I greatly helped those who through God's undeserved kindness had become believers.
Publicly and with great intensity I thoroughly proved the Jews to be wrong.
Some in Corinth said they belonged to me.
I wanted to go across to Achaia, so the brothers wrote urging the disciples to receive me kindly.
While I was in Corinth, Paul came down to Ephesus.
Paul told Titus to send me on my way diligently so that I would lack nothing.
Paul wrote that I was not willing to come to Corinth just then, though he strongly encouraged me.
I came from Italy with my wife Priscilla.
I was a Jew, a native of Pontus.
I was a tentmaker by trade.
Paul stayed at my home and worked with me, since I had the same trade.
Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, so I had recently come from Italy.
I sailed with Paul for Syria, along with Priscilla.
Paul found me in Corinth.
Paul left me in Ephesus.
When I heard Apollos, I took him into my company and helped explain the way of God more accurately.
After Corinth, I was left in Ephesus while Paul went on.
From Ephesus, the congregation that was in my house sent greetings.
Not only Paul but all the congregations of the nations gave thanks for me.
Paul greeted me and Prisca and said I risked my neck for his life.
There was a congregation in my house.
Forced out of Rome by Claudius, I made tents in Corinth and hosted Paul in my trade.
From Corinth I went on to Ephesus, where I helped correct Apollos' understanding of the way.
Paul said I risked my neck for him and that a congregation met in my house.
I was a Macedonian, a traveling companion of Paul.
I was dragged into Ephesus' theater during the disturbance.
I was from Thessalonica.
During the Artemis riot, the crowd rushed into Ephesus' theater dragging Gaius and me.
I sailed with Paul when he put out to sea for Italy.
I was among those who accompanied Paul into Asia.
Paul called me his fellow worker.
I was listed with Sopater, Secundus, Gaius, Timothy, Tychicus, and Trophimus as Paul's travel company.
On the voyage, I was with Paul as a Macedonian of Thessalonica.
Paul called me his fellow captive.
Dragged into Ephesus' theater as Paul's companion, I later sailed with him toward Italy.
As a Thessalonian, I accompanied Paul both toward Asia and on his voyage to Italy.
Paul wrote of me both as a fellow captive and as a fellow worker.
Crowds in Lystra started calling me Zeus.
I came to Saul's aid and led him to the apostles.
I sold a piece of land and deposited the money at the feet of the apostles.
I was a Levite, a native of Cyprus.
I went to Tarsus to make a thorough search for Saul.
The apostles gave me a name that means “Son of Comfort.”
The congregation in Jerusalem sent me as far as Antioch.
The holy spirit said to set Saul and me aside for the work.
After I found Saul, I brought him to Antioch.
After Iconium danger, I fled with Paul toward Lystra and Derbe.
For a whole year Saul and I taught quite a crowd in Antioch.
From Seleucia I sailed away to Cyprus with Saul.
I carried relief to the elders in Judea together with Saul.
I disputed in Antioch against those demanding circumcision for salvation.
I encouraged the believers in Antioch to continue in the Lord with heartfelt resolve.
I said that Paul and I too are humans having the same infirmities as they have.
I told the apostles in detail how Saul had seen the Lord on the road to Damascus.
I was a good man and full of holy spirit and of faith.
I was among the prophets and teachers in Antioch.
I was determined to take along John who was called Mark.
Before the apostles renamed me, I had a different given name.
On Cyprus I proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues, with John as attendant.
When I saw God's undeserved kindness in Antioch, I rejoiced.
When people tried to sacrifice to Paul and me, I ripped my garments and leaped out into the crowd.
After Paul's stoning, on the next day he left with me for Derbe.
After a sharp burst of anger with Paul over Mark, I took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus.
After fasting and prayer, the congregation laid their hands on Saul and me and sent me off.
After persecution there, I shook the dust off my feet and went to Iconium.
Back in Syrian Antioch, I related that God had opened to the nations the door to faith.
I went up to Jerusalem with Paul about the circumcision issue.
In Paphos, Sergius Paulus called for Saul and me to hear the word of God.
In Pisidian Antioch, after the synagogue talk, many followed Paul and me; I urged them to remain in God's undeserved kindness.
It was first in Antioch, while Saul and I taught there, that the disciples were by divine providence called Christians.
Mark was my cousin.
Alongside Paul, I boldly declared a turn to the nations after the Jews rejected the word.
Paul later asked whether only he and I do not have authority to refrain from working for a living.
The apostles and elders called Paul and me “beloved” in their letter.
The whole group listened as Paul and I related signs and wonders God had done among the nations.
I appointed elders in each congregation, praying with fasting.
I returned through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch, strengthening the disciples.
In Antioch I was led along in the hypocrisy when certain men from James came, before Paul resisted Cephas.
James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and me the right hand of sharing, I to the nations and they to the circumcised.
After Jerusalem sent me to Antioch, I searched for Saul in Tarsus and brought him back to teach there with me for a year.
Set aside with Saul by holy spirit, I sailed first to my native Cyprus with John as attendant.
An angel of God came to me in a vision.
I feared God together with all my household.
I lived in Caesarea.
An angel told me to send for Simon who is called Peter.
I was an army officer in what was called the Italian unit.
While Peter was still speaking, the holy spirit came upon those hearing the word in my house.
About the ninth hour of the day, I saw the vision plainly.
I called two of my servants and a devout soldier from among my attendants.
I made many gifts of mercy to the people.
I made supplication to God continually.
I related everything to my household servants and sent them to Joppa.
I stared at the angel, terrified, and asked: “What is it, Lord?”
I was expecting Peter and had called together my relatives and close friends.
I was told Peter was staying as a guest with Simon a tanner by the sea.
The angel said my prayers and gifts of mercy had ascended as a remembrance before God.
When Peter entered, I fell down at his feet and did obeisance to him.
Four days after the vision, counting from that hour, I recounted it to Peter in my house.
I said I and all those with me were present before God to hear all Jehovah had commanded Peter to say.
Messengers said I was a righteous and God-fearing man, well-reported-on by the whole nation of the Jews.
Peter commanded that I be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
Peter lifted me up, saying: “Rise; I too am just a man.”
Those with me spoke in foreign languages and magnified God.
I requested Peter to stay for some days.
I gathered relatives and friends before Peter arrived, then fell at his feet until he raised me as only a man.
In my house people of the nations received holy spirit while Peter was still speaking, then were baptized.
My continual prayers and gifts of mercy brought an angel's order to send for Peter in Joppa.
Peter later reported that an angel told me he would speak things by which my household might get saved.
I abounded in good deeds and gifts of mercy.
I fell sick and died.
I was a disciple in Joppa.
Peter told me to rise, and I opened my eyes and sat up.
After I died, they bathed me and laid me in an upper room.
Disciples sent two men to Lydda to urge Peter to come to me without delay.
Widows showed Peter many garments and robes I had made while I was with them.
Giving me his hand, Peter raised me up.
Peter called the holy ones and the widows and presented me alive.
Peter put everyone outside, knelt, and prayed before turning toward my body.
After I was presented alive, news spread through Joppa and many became believers.
After my death, widows showed Peter the garments I had made.
Laid in an upper room in Joppa, I opened my eyes when Peter told me to rise.
I opposed Barnabas and Saul.
I was a false prophet.
I was a sorcerer.
I was struck blind for a time.
A thick mist and darkness fell on me.
I tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
I was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus.
I went around trying to find someone to lead me by the hand.
My other name is a translation of my given name.
I met Barnabas and Saul at Paphos on Cyprus.
Jehovah's hand was upon me, and I would not see the sunlight for a time.
Paul called me a son of the Devil and an enemy of everything righteous.
Paul said I was distorting the right ways of Jehovah.
Paul said I was full of every sort of fraud and villainy.
At Paphos I tried to turn the proconsul away, and mist and darkness fell on me.
Called a fraud and enemy of righteousness, I went blind under Jehovah's hand.
Opposing the faith before Sergius Paulus, I was left groping for a hand to lead me.
I fell sick nearly to the point of death.
Paul said that I nearly died on account of the work of Christ.
Paul called me his brother, fellow worker and fellow soldier.
God had mercy on me in my sickness.
I risked my life to make up for the Philippians' not being there to render personal service to Paul.
I was depressed because the Philippians heard that I had fallen sick.
I was longing to see the Philippians.
Paul called me the Philippians' envoy and personal servant for his need.
Paul received from me what the Philippians sent.
Paul considered it necessary to send me with the greatest urgency to the Philippians so they could rejoice again.
Paul said to keep holding men of my sort dear.
Paul told the Philippians to give me the customary welcome in the Lord with all joy.
I fell down from the third story.
I sank into a deep sleep while Paul kept talking.
I was a young man.
I was picked up dead.
They took me away alive.
I was seated at a window in the upper room.
Overcome by sleep, I fell.
Paul threw himself on me and embraced me.
After I was restored, they were comforted beyond measure.
Paul prolonged his speech until midnight before I fell.
Paul said concerning me, “Stop making a commotion, for he is alive.”
There were quite a few lamps in the upper room where I sat listening to Paul.
After I fell three stories in Troas, Paul embraced me, and I later came back to life.
I was picked up dead, but later they took me away alive and were comforted beyond measure.
Overcome by deep sleep as Paul prolonged his speech, I fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
I became frightened as Paul talked.
I left Paul in custody.
I listened to Paul speak about the belief in Christ Jesus.
I was the governor.
Paul was brought safely to me.
After two years I was succeeded by Porcius Festus.
Claudius Lysias wrote to me as His Excellency the governor.
I allowed Paul's people to attend to his needs.
I asked what province Paul was from and learned he was from Cilicia.
I came with Drusilla my wife, who was Jewish.
I commanded that Paul be kept under guard in Herod's palace.
I hoped Paul would give me money.
I ordered Paul kept under arrest but given some freedom.
I said I would give Paul a thorough hearing when his accusers arrived.
Knowing quite well the facts concerning this Way, I put them off.
Because I desired to gain favor with the Jews, I left Paul in custody.
Hoping Paul would give me money, I sent for him frequently and conversed with him.
I nodded to Paul to speak in his defense.
I put the case off until Lysias the military commander would come down.
I said, “Go away for now, but when I have an opportunity I will send for you again.”
Paul talked before me about righteousness and self-control and the judgment to come.
Hearing righteousness, self-control, and judgment, I grew frightened and sent Paul away.
Hoping for money, I talked with Paul often, then left him bound to please the Jews.
Knowing the Way well, I delayed judgment and kept Paul under guard with some freedom.
I presented Paul's case to King Agrippa.
I said, “To Caesar you have appealed; to Caesar you will go.”
I succeeded Felix as governor.
Paul appealed to Caesar before me.
After speaking with the assembly of counselors, I confirmed the appeal to Caesar.
Desiring to gain favor with the Jews, I asked if Paul wished to go up to Jerusalem.
I answered that Paul was to be kept in Caesarea.
I perceived that Paul had done nothing deserving of death.
I said great learning was driving Paul out of his mind.
I sat down on the judgment seat and commanded Paul to be brought in.
I told Agrippa Paul had been left as a prisoner by Felix.
The chief priests and principal men of the Jews gave me information against Paul.
Three days after arriving in the province, I went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
Agrippa told me Paul could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.
Being at a loss how to handle the dispute, I asked about judgment in Jerusalem.
I had nothing certain to write about Paul to my Lord.
I refused to hand Paul over before he met his accusers face-to-face, citing Roman procedure.
I said it seemed unreasonable to send a prisoner without indicating the charges.
I said the Jews had disputes about their own worship of the deity and about Jesus, whom Paul asserted was alive.
Paul's accusers charged none of the wicked things I had expected.
At a loss over disputes about Jesus alive, I still found nothing deserving of death.
Seeking Jewish favor, I offered Jerusalem judgment; Paul answered with an appeal to Caesar.
With Agrippa, Bernice, military commanders, and prominent men assembled, I commanded Paul to be brought in.
I rose in the Sanhedrin.
I was a Law teacher.
I was a Pharisee.
Paul was educated at my feet.
I commanded that the men be put outside for a little while.
I recalled Judas the Galilean in the days of the registration.
I recalled Theudas, who rose up saying he himself was somebody.
I said if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them.
I said if the work is from men, it will be overthrown.
I warned they might even be found fighters against God himself.
I warned, “Men of Israel, be careful as to what you intend to do about these men.”
I was esteemed by all the people.
After taking my advice, they still flogged the apostles and ordered them to stop speaking.
I reminded the Sanhedrin that about 400 men joined Theudas before his party came to nothing.
I reminded them that Judas the Galilean drew followers after himself and then perished.
Paul said he was instructed at my feet according to the strictness of the ancestral Law.
Esteemed Law teacher in the Sanhedrin, I told Israel to be careful about these men.
I warned that opposing a work from God could make them fighters against God.
Using Theudas and Judas as warnings, I urged: let them alone.
I sent greetings along with Paul's letter.
I traveled with Paul.
I was Paul's fellow worker.
I was the beloved physician.
Only I was with Paul.
A servant girl with a demon kept following Paul and me.
After Paul's Macedonian vision, I tried to go into Macedonia with him.
Aristarchus a Macedonian was with me as I sailed for Italy with Paul.
In Troas I was gathered in an upper room when Eutychus fell.
Lydia urged me to stay at her house.
On the Sabbath I went beside a river to a place of prayer.
I began speaking to the women who had assembled.
I drew the conclusion that God had summoned me to declare the good news.
I put out to sea from Troas and came to Philippi.
I went ahead by ship and set sail for Assos.
I was handed over with Paul to the army officer Julius.
In the same letter that calls Mark Barnabas's cousin, I was the beloved physician.
Paul named me with Demas when sending Colossian greetings.
Paul named me with Mark, Aristarchus, and Demas among his fellow workers.
I arrived in Rome with Paul after the voyage.
I navigated with Paul toward Rome and endured the storm and shipwreck voyage.
I stayed in Philippi for some days.
When others had gone elsewhere, Paul wrote that only I was with him.
Concluding God had summoned me, I crossed from Troas to Philippi's place of prayer.
I sailed with Paul and Aristarchus when Julius took the prisoners for Italy.
Named Paul's beloved physician and fellow worker, I was later the only one still with him.
Traveling with Paul, I was among those Lydia constrained to stay at her house.
I was a seller of purple.
Jehovah opened my heart wide to pay attention to the things Paul was saying.
My household and I got baptized after I listened to Paul speak.
I urged Paul and Silas: “If you have considered me to be faithful to Jehovah, come and stay at my house.”
The writer of Acts said of me "she just made us come."
I was a worshipper of God from the city of Thyatira..
I was among the women assembled on the Sabbath, outside the gate beside a river.
My conversion happened at Philippi, a colony and principal city of the district of Macedonia.
After Paul and Silas left prison in Philippi, they came to my home.
At my home Paul and Silas saw the brothers and encouraged them.
Barnabas took me along and sailed away to Cyprus.
I left Paul and Barnabas and returned to Jerusalem.
I was an attendant to Barnabas and Saul.
Paul later said I was helpful to him in the ministry.
Barnabas and Saul took me along with them from Jerusalem.
Barnabas was determined to take me along.
I was the cousin of Barnabas.
I departed from Paul and Barnabas in Pamphylia and did not go with them to the work.
My mother was Mary, and believers gathered at her house to pray.
Paul gave instructions that the Colossians welcome me if I came.
Paul named me among his fellow workers.
Paul was not in favor of taking me along.
Peter called me his son.
After the split, I sailed to Cyprus with Barnabas, not with Paul and Silas.
Among those circumcised, Paul said men like me had become a source of great comfort to him.
From earlier rejection to later request, Paul told Timothy to bring me along.
On Cyprus I served as attendant while Barnabas and Saul proclaimed in the synagogues.
Paul's objection specifically recalled my departure in Pamphylia.
Peter came to my mother's house after an angel led him out of prison.
There was a sharp burst of anger over taking me along, so that Barnabas and Paul separated.
After leaving the work in Pamphylia, I became the reason Barnabas insisted and Paul refused.
Cousin of Barnabas and welcomed by name, I also stood among Paul's fellow workers.
Once not favored for the trip, I was later called helpful and asked for by Paul.
The sharp burst of anger over me sent me to Cyprus with Barnabas.
I was a slave.
Paul became a father to me while he was in prison.
Paul called me his child.
Paul sent me back to my master.
I was from among the Colossians.
I became useful to my master and to Paul.
I broke away from my master for a short while.
I was formerly useless to my master.
Paul asked that I be received as more than a slave, as a beloved brother.
I traveled with Tychicus and was to tell the Colossians the things happening with Paul.
Paul called me his very own heart.
Paul said that if I did my master any wrong or owed him anything, it should be charged to Paul's account.
Paul wanted to keep me so I might take my master's place in ministering to him in prison.
Paul would not keep me without my master's consent.
After I broke away, Paul sent me back so my master might have me forever, no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother.
As a faithful and beloved brother from among the Colossians, I traveled with Tychicus.
Paul, who became my father in prison, sent me back as his own heart rather than keep me without consent.
A violent earthquake shook the prison where I was held.
A voice asked why I was persecuting him, repeating my name.
At Philippi I was praying and praising God at midnight in prison.
At Troas I raised Eutychus after he fell from the third story.
For three days I neither ate nor drank.
I was a Roman by birth.
I appealed to Caesar.
I asked the high priest for letters to bring followers of The Way bound to Jerusalem.
I breathed threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord.
I once persecuted the congregation of God.
I was a Pharisee.
I was a tentmaker.
I was born in Tarsus of Cilicia.
I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.
I was led by the hand into Damascus because I could see nothing.
In Damascus I began to preach that Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus told me I was persecuting him.
Near Damascus a light from heaven flashed around me.
On the voyage to Rome my ship was wrecked.
What looked like scales fell from my eyes, and I was baptized.
After Jerusalem, the brothers sent me away to Tarsus.
After her owners lost their profit, I was beaten with rods and thrown into prison.
Agabus took my belt and bound his own feet and hands.
Agrippa said to me: “In a short time you would persuade me to become a Christian.”
Ananias laid his hands on me so that I might recover sight and be filled with holy spirit.
At Antioch the holy spirit said to set Barnabas and me apart for the work.
At Cenchreae I had my hair clipped short because of a vow I had made.
At Lystra the crowds called me Hermes, because I was the principal speaker.
At Miletus I called the older men of the Ephesus congregation to me.
At Philippi I spoke to the women gathered at the place of prayer.
Barnabas came to Tarsus looking for me and brought me to Antioch.
Barnabas took me and brought me to the apostles.
Before Agrippa I said I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
Demetrius the silversmith stirred up a riot against me over the temple of Artemis.
Felix hoped I would give him money, so he sent for me often.
I circumcised Timothy because of the Jews in those places.
I commanded a demon to come out of a girl who had a spirit of prediction.
I entered house after house, dragging out men and women and turning them over to prison.
I refused to leave Philippi quietly after being beaten as a Roman.
I said I was ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
I stopped the Philippian jailer when he was about to kill himself.
I told the jailer: “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
I told those older men I had not held back from telling them all the counsel of God.
In Athens I was irritated at seeing the city full of idols.
In Corinth I stayed with Aquila and Priscilla and worked at the same trade.
In Ephesus many who practiced magical arts burned their books publicly while I was there.
In a vision a Macedonian man pleaded with me to step over and help.
In a vision the Lord told me not to be afraid to keep speaking in Corinth.
In the temple I was seized while completing the days of the purification.
Lydia and her household were baptized after Jehovah opened her heart to my message.
My sister's son heard of the plot to ambush me and reported it.
On Cyprus I called Elymas a son of the Devil and announced that Jehovah's hand would make him blind temporarily.
On Malta I healed the father of Publius of fever and dysentery.
On the Areopagus I spoke about the God who made the world and about the resurrection.
When I tried to join the disciples in Jerusalem, they were all afraid of me.
When Stephen's blood was spilled, I stood by approving and guarded the outer garments of those killing him.
A thorn in the flesh was given me, an angel of Satan to keep slapping me.
After a sharp burst of anger, Barnabas took Mark and sailed away, and I chose Silas.
After my calling I went off into Arabia, then returned to Damascus.
At Lystra, after healing a man lame from birth, I tore my garments when the crowds tried to sacrifice to me.
At Miletus I said I knew that imprisonment and tribulations awaited me in Jerusalem.
At Paphos the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed after Elymas became blind.
At Philippi I was dragged before the civil magistrates and accused of advocating unlawful customs.
Berean Jews examined the Scriptures daily to see whether the things I said were so.
From prison I wrote about Onesimus, once useless, now useful.
I was of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews.
I asked Philemon to charge any wrong of Onesimus to my account.
I baptized Crispus and Gaius, and also the household of Stephanas.
I counted all my former gains as a lot of refuse so that I might gain Christ.
I decided to know nothing among the Corinthians except Jesus Christ, and him executed on the torture stake.
I wrote that I had 'fought with wild beasts at Ephesus.'
I handed a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh so that the spirit might be saved.
I left Troas though a door was opened for me in the Lord, because I was concerned about Titus.
I said I would rather speak five words with my mind than ten thousand words in a tongue.
I told the Ephesian older men that from among them men would rise and speak twisted things.
I was caught away to the third heaven—whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know.
I was praying on the street called Straight when Ananias was sent to me.
I went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas over the circumcision issue.
I worked with my own hands so as not to be an expensive burden.
In Athens some said I seemed to be a proclaimer of foreign deities.
In Jerusalem, while praying in the temple, I fell into a trance and was told to leave quickly.
In Thessalonica a mob searched for me at Jason's house.
James and Cephas and John gave Barnabas and me the right hand of sharing.
More than forty men bound themselves with a curse neither to eat nor drink until they had killed me.
Of the apostles I saw no one else except James the brother of the Lord.
On the voyage I urged all to take a meal, saying not a hair of anyone's head would perish.
Three times I begged the Lord that the thorn in my flesh might depart from me.
Three years later I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas and stayed with him fifteen days.
Titus was with me, and even he was not compelled to be circumcised.
When Gallio was proconsul, the Jews accused me, but he drove them away from the judgment seat.
When the high priest Ananias ordered me struck, I called him a whitewashed wall—then apologized, not knowing he was high priest.
After my Macedonian vision, Lydia and her household were baptized in Philippi.
A viper fastened on my hand after the wreck; when I neither swelled up nor died, the Maltese changed their minds and said I was a god.
After Barnabas and I split over Mark, I went through Syria and Cilicia with Silas, strengthening the congregations.
After being flogged uncondemned, I made the magistrates come and escort me out by citing my Roman citizenship.
After persecuting The Way to the point of death, I was told in the temple trance that I would be sent to nations far away.
Agabus bound himself with my belt to show how I would be bound; I still went up to Jerusalem ready even to die.
At Lystra I was stoned and left for dead outside the city; the next day I left with Barnabas for Derbe.
At Miletus I told the older men I was innocent of the blood of all men, having declared the whole counsel of God, though bonds awaited me.
Beaten and jailed at Philippi for casting out a spirit of prediction, I sang praises until an earthquake opened the doors.
Before Agrippa I retold the Damascus light and the heavenly commission; he said I was nearly persuading him to become a Christian.
Before the Sanhedrin I split Pharisees from Sadducees by confessing hope in the resurrection of the dead.
Blinded by heavenly light on the road to Damascus, I recovered sight when Ananias laid his hands on me, and I was baptized.
Caught away to the third heaven and shown things unutterable, I was afterward given a thorn in the flesh so I would not be overly exalted.
Completing a purification in the temple to quiet rumors, I was seized on the charge of bringing Greeks into the sanctuary.
Felix left me in custody to gain favor with the Jews; when Festus later proposed a Jerusalem trial, I appealed to Caesar.
